gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Intel Celeron N5095 (QNAP TS-464), N5105 (Asustor AS6704T v2 / AS5402T) and J4125 (Synology DS225+ / DS425+) list only SSE4.2 on Intel's spec pages, with no AVX, so the official Frigate 0.17 image crashes on them with an 'illegal instruction' error, because Frigate's FAQ says 0.17 needs a CPU with AVX.
standout_why: I compared this against docs.frigate.video/frigate/hardware (cited in every chat), the GitHub dev copy of hardware.md, and docs.frigate.video/frigate/installation (cited). They state the rule, 'Anything with an Intel CPU (with AVX + AVX2 instructions)', but name no NAS CPU. The installation page covers only QNAP's Container Station limits (no GHCR, 64 MB shm) and Synology's 'high privilege' switch, not the CPU. ChatGPT repeated the AVX caveat in chat 1 and still recommended the QNAP TS-464 there and in four other chats. It also recommended the Asustor AS6704T v2. None of the results maps a recommended NAS's CPU to the AVX rule.
decides: This takes the QNAP TS-464, Asustor AS6704T v2 and AS5402T, and Synology DS225+ / DS425+ out of the running for official Frigate 0.17 and later. The only route left on them is an unofficial community 'oldcpu' image. The Alder Lake picks have AVX2 according to Intel: the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus (Pentium Gold 8505) and the N100 boxes (UGREEN DXP2800 and DXP4800, Beelink EQ13). That makes the DXP4800 Plus the top pick and the DXP2800 the budget pick. Our current page has to drop or flag its TS-464, DS225+ and AS5402T rows, which wrongly show 'OpenVINO; Coral USB' as working.

findings.label: Frigate 0.17 CPU requirement (developer FAQ)
findings.value: "Frigate 0.17 requires a modern CPU with AVX (Advanced Vector Extensions) instructions." The FAQ lists the cause of an 'illegal instruction' crash as "Your CPU lacks AVX instructions required by TensorFlow"
findings.note: Started by hawkeye217 and described as 'maintained by the Frigate developers'. Posted 2025-12-14, updated 2026-03-05. Listed under 'Upgrade issues', item 3.

findings.label: Frigate hardware doc CPU rule
findings.value: "Anything with an Intel CPU (with AVX + AVX2 instructions) and capable of running Debian should work fine."
findings.note: This page is cited by ChatGPT. It names no NAS or Celeron model. Same sentence in the GitHub dev copy of hardware.md.

findings.label: Face recognition CPU requirement
findings.value: "A CPU with AVX + AVX2 instructions is required to run Face Recognition."
findings.note: This adds AVX2 on top of the base AVX need.

findings.label: What happens without AVX, and the only workaround
findings.value: "If you try to run the official Frigate docker image on a CPU that doesn't support AVX instructions, it will crash." A community-maintained custom image exists. The same author warns that "CPUs this old are unlikely to handle object detection for more than one or two cameras."
findings.note: Post dated 2025-04-26. The image is unofficial, not a Frigate project build.

findings.note: The QNAP page lists AES-NI as its only instruction-set item.

findings.note: Taken with the 0.17 FAQ, the official image will not run. This also applies to the QNAP TS-264-8G, which uses the same N5095.

A first-hand Frigate GitHub issue showing the illegal-instruction crash on a TS-464, DS225+/DS425+ or AS6704T specifically: none turned up. The conclusion rests on Intel's instruction-set lists plus Frigate's FAQ.
